newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Austrian far right gains worrisome, Martens says.
newsitem.headline: Austrian far right gains worrisome, Martens says.

text.p: The head of the European Parliament's conservative European People's Party said on Monday he was worried about the gains made by the far right Freedom Party in Austria's election on Sunday.
But Wilfried Martens, a former Belgian prime minister, said it would have little impact on the European Parliament's daily workings.
Martens said in a statement that he had sent a congratulatory letter to Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel, whose conservative People's Party won an extra seat in the parliament.
He said he had also expressed concern about growing Euroscepticism and the Freedom Party's showing in the election.
"However, the gain of one seat registered by this party will not have any influence on the daily activities of the (European Parliament)," he said.
The populist Freedom Party snatched almost 28 percent of the vote in Sunday's poll, just 60,000 votes behind Chancellor Franz Vranitzky's Social Democrats with 29.1 percent.
That translates into six of Austria's 21 seats in the European Parliament -- up from five before the election.
Schuessel's People's Party won 29.6 percent. It will have seven seats in the European parliament -- up from six.
Those deputies will be part of the European People's Party (PPE) group in the parliament -- with 174 members, the assembly's second-largest group behind the Socialists.
"The People's Party's electoral victory proves the pro-European strategy promoted by the PPE was well founded," Martens said.
